data.name: ReadOnly.Title
data.value: View-only mode: you can see backup status, but you cannot run or change jobs.

data.name: ReadOnly.Elevate
data.value: Your account is an administrator, but Kobian is running without elevated rights. Close the app and start it again with “Run as administrator”.

data.name: ReadOnly.AskOperator
data.value: To run backups, ask the computer’s administrator to add your account to the “Kobian Operators” group.

data.name: Retention.Held
data.value: Cleanup of old backups is paused — a large system clock jump was detected. New backups run as usual.

data.name: Retention.Held.Admin
data.value: Check the computer date and time, then confirm resuming with:

data.name: Retention.Held.Other
data.value: Ask an administrator to check the clock and confirm resuming cleanup.

data.name: Connection.Lost
data.value: No connection to the Kobian service. Data may be out of date.

data.name: Hero.Empty
data.value: You have no backup jobs yet

data.name: Hero.EmptyHint
data.value: The wizard takes about 5 minutes and ends with a test restore of one file.

data.name: Nav.ComingSoon
data.value: This screen arrives in a later version.

data.name: Reason.Disabled
data.value: Job disabled — no backups are made.

data.name: Reason.HostKeyMismatch
data.value: The server presented a different key than remembered. Backups are held for safety.

data.name: Reason.LowSpace
data.value: {0}% free space left on the destination.

data.name: Reason.NotDeleteProtected
data.value: The destination does not protect backups from deletion (e.g. ransomware).

data.name: Reason.NotVerified
data.value: The last backup is not verified yet.

data.name: Reason.RepositoryDamaged
data.value: The repository on the destination is damaged. The next backup will be full.

data.name: Reason.V3Overdue
data.value: Periodic data check on the destination is overdue.

data.name: Reason.OkTile
data.value: Backups run on schedule and are verified.

data.name: Offline.Headline
data.value: The Kobian service is not running

data.name: Offline.Detail
data.value: No backups are made until the service is started.

data.name: Offline.Denied.Headline
data.value: No access to the Kobian service

data.name: Offline.Denied.Detail
data.value: The service is running, but your account has no access to it. Ask an administrator to add you to the “Kobian Operators” or “Kobian Admins” group, then sign out and back in (or run the app as administrator).

data.name: Failure.Reference
data.value: Reference: {0} — details in the service log agent-errors.log (Windows: C:\ProgramData\Kobian\logs, Linux: /var/lib/kobian/logs).

data.name: Jobs.Paused
data.value: Schedule of “{0}” paused — manual runs still work.

data.name: Jobs.Subtitle
data.value: All backup jobs — state, schedule and last successful backup.

data.name: History.EmptyHint
data.value: The first backup will appear here after the job runs.

data.name: History.Truncated
data.value: Showing the 500 most recent entries — pick a job to narrow the list.

data.name: Reason.SchedulePaused
data.value: Schedule paused — automatic backups are not running.

data.name: Wizard.S1.Hint
data.value: Add at least one folder. Subfolders of a selected folder are protected automatically.

data.name: Wizard.S2.SmbCredential
data.value: Credential (entry name in the service secret store)

data.name: Wizard.S2.SmbHint
data.value: Enter the folder as a UNC path, e.g. \\nas\backups\office. The share password is stored by an administrator in the service secret store — the wizard does not accept it.

data.name: Wizard.S2.Hint
data.value: Preferably a different drive than the protected data. After “Next” we check that the destination is reachable and writable.

data.name: Wizard.Identity.Hint
data.value: This is the first connection to this server. Compare the key fingerprint with the one from the server administrator — approve only if they match.

data.name: Wizard.Schedule.ManualHint
data.value: Backup only when you click “Run now” — the dashboard will not warn about overdue backups.

data.name: Wizard.Schedule.BadTime
data.value: Enter the time as HH:MM, e.g. 21:00.

data.name: Wizard.S4.Hint
data.value: Backups are encrypted. Without the password or the recovery key nobody — including support — can restore the data. At least 12 characters; a few words work best.

data.name: Wizard.Security.Mismatch
data.value: The passwords differ — type the same password in both fields.

data.name: Wizard.Key.Hint
data.value: It is the only way to recover data if the password is lost. Write it on paper and keep it away from the computer. To continue, type the two indicated groups.

data.name: Wizard.Key.Mismatch
data.value: The typed groups do not match the key. Check your copy and try again.

data.name: Wizard.S5.Hint
data.value: Backups outside these rules are marked for removal during cleanup (preview first). Each rule keeps the newest backup of its period.

data.name: Wizard.Final.Protected
data.value: First backup completed and verified. Your data is protected.

data.name: Wizard.Final.Saved
data.value: Job saved. The first backup will run on schedule.

data.name: Wizard.Final.Failed
data.value: Job saved, but the first backup failed: {0}

data.name: Wizard.Retention.Preview
data.value: Once settled: about {0}, the oldest from {1} ago

data.name: Wizard.Db.Hint
data.value: The Agent connects to the server and only reads the list of databases. The copy is made with BACKUP WITH CHECKSUM — the database keeps working meanwhile.

data.name: Wizard.Db.Credential
data.value: Name of the SQL credential in the Agent

data.name: Wizard.Db.CredentialHint
data.value: The Agent stores the login and password (secrets folder) — the wizard never sees them.

data.name: Wizard.Db.SelectFirst
data.value: Choose a database from the list — click “Show databases” first.

data.name: Wizard.Db.ScriptHint
data.value: Give this script to the SQL Server administrator: it grants the Kobian service account only the right to make backups.

data.name: Wizard.Db.CertHint
data.value: Compare the SHA-256 fingerprint with the SQL Server administrator (SQL Server Configuration Manager → Protocols → Certificate). Approve only if it matches — the Agent will remember this certificate and reject any other.

data.name: Wizard.Db.CertTrusted
data.value: trusted by the system — approval optional

data.name: Browse.EmptyHint
data.value: After the first backup you can browse and restore its contents here.

data.name: Browse.Truncated
data.value: Showing the first 5,000 entries — restore the folder to get all files.

data.name: Restore.TargetHint
data.value: An existing folder on the computer running the Kobian service, e.g. D:\Restored. The path inside the backup is kept.

data.name: Restore.TargetInvalid
data.value: Enter the full path of an existing folder (e.g. D:\Restored).

data.name: Restore.NoOverwrite
data.value: Existing files are never overwritten — they are skipped and listed in the result. Links are not restored.

data.name: Restore.Plan.Conflicts
data.value: Skipped — already in the destination folder and never overwritten: {0}

data.name: Restore.Planning
data.value: Checking the backup and the destination folder…

data.name: Restore.Plan.Resumable
data.value: From an interrupted attempt: {0} already restored — will be skipped without conflict.

data.name: Restore.RunningPlan
data.value: Restoring: {0} ({1})… Every file is verified with a checksum.

data.name: Restore.Running
data.value: Restoring… Every file is checked against its checksum.

data.name: Restore.Done.Ok
data.value: Restored — all files match the backup.

data.name: Settings.RestartNeeded
data.value: The new language appears after restarting the application.

data.name: Settings.AuditHint
data.value: Checks that no recorded operation was changed (SHA-256 hash chain).

data.name: Settings.AnchorHint
data.value: Store it off the server (e.g. in a ticket). Later: kobian audit verify --anchor <anchor> detects a rewritten or truncated log.

data.name: Settings.AuditBroken
data.value: Log changed outside the application from entry {0}.

data.name: Settings.Offline
data.value: No connection to the service — only this computer's settings are shown.

data.name: Settings.LocalNote
data.value: Appearance and language apply only to your account on this computer.

data.name: Runtime.Unpatched
data.value: The service runs on an unpatched .NET — backups work, but install the .NET 10 update.

data.name: Settings.RuntimeBad
data.value: unpatched: {0} ({1}) — install the .NET 10 update and restart the service

data.name: Dest.Unreadable
data.value: Could not read job definitions: {0} — check them in the job list.

data.name: Dest.SpaceUnknown
data.value: Connection works — the destination does not report free space.

data.name: Dest.EmptyHint
data.value: A destination appears here after you create the first job.

data.name: Dest.Note
data.value: Destinations come from jobs. Adding and editing destinations and credentials — in a later version.

data.name: DbRestore.TargetHint
data.value: The database is created next to the existing ones on the same SQL Server. The production database is not changed.

data.name: DbRestore.NameInvalid
data.value: Database name: up to 128 characters, no control characters.

data.name: DbRestore.NoOverwrite
data.value: An existing database is never overwritten — if the name is taken, the restore stops with a message (KB-3501).

data.name: DbRestore.Running
data.value: Restoring the database… The backup file is checked with checksums.

data.name: Browse.Damage.Unrecoverable
data.value: This backup cannot be restored (result of check with repair). Choose another backup from the list.

data.name: Browse.Damage.Partial
data.value: This backup is partially damaged — cannot be restored: {0}. Other files and folders restore normally.

data.name: Wizard.WebDav.Hint
data.value: The connection is always encrypted (HTTPS). Works with Nextcloud, ownCloud, Synology/QNAP NAS and Apache/nginx WebDAV servers.

data.name: Wizard.WebDav.PathHint
data.value: Folder path in the WebDAV address, starting with “/” (Nextcloud: /remote.php/dav/files/<user>/<folder>). The folder must exist. After “Next” we check the connection, the server certificate and write access.

data.name: Wizard.Ftps.ModeHint
data.value: Both modes encrypt the password and data. If unsure, keep “Standard”; choose port 990 only when the server manual or administrator says so.

data.name: Wizard.Ftps.Credential
data.value: Credential (entry name in the service secret store)

data.name: Wizard.Ftps.CredentialHint
data.value: The server login and password are stored by an administrator in the service secret store — the wizard does not accept them. An account without delete rights is recommended.

data.name: Wizard.Ftps.PathHint
data.value: Folder on the server, starting with “/”. After “Next” we check the connection, the server certificate and write access.

data.name: Wizard.Ftps.PlainFtp
data.value: Plain FTP without encryption is not available in the wizard — the password and data would travel in clear text. Use FTPS or SFTP.

data.name: Wizard.Ftps.Err.HostRequired
data.value: Enter the server name or address.

data.name: Wizard.Ftps.Err.HostScheme
data.value: Enter just the server name, without “ftp://”, “ftps://” or “https://”.

data.name: Wizard.Ftps.Err.HostPath
data.value: Enter just the server name — put the folder below, in “Destination folder”.

data.name: Wizard.Ftps.Err.HostUser
data.value: Enter just the server name, without a user and “@” — the login is in the credential.

data.name: Wizard.Ftps.Err.HostPort
data.value: Enter just the server name — put the port in the “Port” field.

data.name: Wizard.Ftps.Err.HostInvalid
data.value: The server name may contain only letters, digits, dots and hyphens (or an IP address).

data.name: Wizard.Ftps.Err.Port
data.value: The port must be a number from 1 to 65535.

data.name: Wizard.Ftps.Err.PathRequired
data.value: Enter the folder on the server, e.g. /backups/office.

data.name: Wizard.Ftps.Err.PathAbsolute
data.value: The server folder must start with “/” and use “/” separators, e.g. /backups/office.

data.name: Wizard.Ftps.Err.PathDotDot
data.value: The folder must not contain “..” (going up to a parent folder).

data.name: Wizard.Ftps.Err.PathInvalid
data.value: The folder contains characters that are not allowed or is too long.

data.name: Wizard.Ftps.Err.CredentialRequired
data.value: Enter the credential entry name from the service secret store.

data.name: Wizard.Ftps.Err.CredentialInvalid
data.value: Entry name: letters, digits, “.”, “_”, “-” (up to 64 characters), no “..”.

data.name: Wizard.Ftps.Identity.Hint
data.value: The system does not trust this server's certificate (e.g. a self-signed certificate or a connection by IP address). Compare the certificate key fingerprint with the one from the server administrator — approve only if they match. The approved fingerprint is saved in the job and survives certificate renewal with the same key.

data.name: Wizard.Ftps.Identity.AdminHint
data.value: The administrator can read the fingerprint on the server with the command from the “FTPS destination” guide. A different fingerprint = do not approve; go back and check the server address.

data.name: Dest.Ftps.NoDetails
data.value: TLS encryption — mode and certificate fingerprint are stored in the job definition

data.name: Dest.CheckUnavailable
data.value: Checking this destination from the list comes in a later service version (the list does not include the server address yet). The wizard and the first backup check the connection.

data.name: Alert.A03
data.value: No successful backup for longer than the schedule allows

data.name: Alert.A04
data.value: Verification found a damaged backup repository

data.name: Alert.A06
data.value: Backup destination is running out of space

data.name: Alert.A07
data.value: A backup disappeared from the destination outside retention

data.name: Alert.A08
data.value: Retention or schedule changed, or a backup was deleted

data.name: Alert.A09
data.value: The destination server key or certificate changed

data.name: Alert.A10
data.value: The destination does not protect against deletion

data.name: Alert.A12
data.value: The Kobian service is not responding

data.name: Alert.A13
data.value: A certificate or secret is about to expire

data.name: Alert.A15
data.value: Failed step-up or repeated API denials

data.name: Alert.A16
data.value: Operating system or SQL Server is out of vendor support

data.name: Alert.A17
data.value: System clock jump — backup cleanup paused

data.name: Progress.Reconnecting
data.value: Lost the connection to the service — retrying {0} of {1}…

data.name: Progress.Lost
data.value: Progress can no longer be read. The run may still be going on in the service — check History.

data.name: Progress.Stopped
data.value: Stopped watching. The run continues in the service.

data.name: Progress.StopNote
data.value: This does not stop the run — the service finishes it in the background.
